# SPI Command Parser Behavioral Specification

## 1. Purpose

The SPI command parser decodes the first byte of an SPI flash transaction and decides which internal processing path, if any, must handle the transaction. It is active only in SPI Flash mode and SPI Passthrough mode. In all other SPI modes it shall remain idle and shall not select any datapath.

## 2. General Behavior

- The parser shall accept a byte only when the SPI interface indicates that a complete byte has been received.
- The parser shall compare that byte with the configured command information entries.
- A command information entry shall contain at least:
  - a valid flag,
  - an opcode,
  - an upload enable flag,
  - address, dummy, payload, and direction parameters used by other logic.
- Opcode matching shall be exact over all eight bits.
- An entry with its valid flag cleared shall be ignored.
- The parser shall not parse address, dummy, or payload phases. It only classifies the opcode.

## 3. Command Classification

The parser shall assign fixed roles to specific command information entries:

- The first three entries are read-status command slots.
- The next entry is the Read JEDEC ID slot.
- The next entry is the Read SFDP slot.
- The next group of entries are read-command slots.
- Dedicated entries are provided for:
  - Enter 4-byte address mode,
  - Exit 4-byte address mode,
  - Write enable,
  - Write disable.
- All other entries may be used for command upload. An entry of this kind shall be treated as an upload command only when its upload flag is set.

If multiple entries match the received opcode, the parser shall apply a fixed priority. The priority order shall be:

1. Read status
2. Read JEDEC ID
3. Read SFDP
4. Read command
5. Command upload
6. Enter/exit 4-byte address mode
7. Write enable/write disable

## 4. Behavior by SPI Mode

### 4.1 Flash Mode

In Flash mode, the parser shall internally process the following command classes:

- Read status commands: shall select the read-status datapath.
- Read JEDEC ID command: shall select the JEDEC ID datapath.
- Read SFDP command: shall select the SFDP datapath.
- Read commands: shall select the read-command datapath.
- Upload commands: shall select the upload datapath.
- Enter/exit 4-byte address mode: shall select the corresponding address-mode datapath.
- Write enable/write disable: shall select the corresponding write-enable or write-disable datapath.

No interception indicator shall be asserted in Flash mode.

### 4.2 Passthrough Mode

In Passthrough mode, the parser shall behave as follows:

- Read status commands shall be processed internally only if the status interception enable is set. Otherwise, they shall not be processed and the parser shall wait for reset.
- Read JEDEC ID commands shall be processed internally only if the JEDEC interception enable is set. Otherwise, they shall not be processed and the parser shall wait for reset.
- Read SFDP commands shall be processed internally only if the SFDP interception enable is set. Otherwise, they shall not be processed and the parser shall wait for reset.
- Read commands shall always be directed to the read-command datapath, regardless of the interception enables.
- Upload commands shall be directed to the upload datapath.
- Enter/exit 4-byte address mode shall be directed to the corresponding address-mode datapath.
- Write enable/write disable shall be directed to the corresponding write-enable or write-disable datapath.

When a read-status, JEDEC, or SFDP command is internally processed in Passthrough mode, the parser shall assert the corresponding interception indicator.

## 5. Datapath Selection

- At most one datapath shall be selected at any time.
- For read status, JEDEC ID, SFDP, read command, and upload commands, the selected datapath shall remain selected until the parser is reset.
- For enter/exit 4-byte address mode and write enable/write disable commands, the datapath shall be asserted at the same time the opcode byte completes. After that, no datapath shall remain selected while the parser waits for the transaction to end.
- If the received byte does not match any valid command information entry, the parser shall select no datapath and shall wait for reset.
- If a valid entry matches but its class is not one of the built-in commands and its upload flag is clear, the parser shall select no datapath and shall wait for reset.

## 6. Command Information Output

- When a valid command entry matches the received byte, the parser shall provide the full matched command information entry and the index of the matched entry.
- This output shall be available in the same cycle that the opcode byte completes.
- The matched entry and index shall also be latched and held until the next matching command is received.
- If no valid match is received, the command information output shall not indicate a valid match.
- The index output shall be meaningful only when a valid match is indicated.

## 7. Interception Indicators

- Interception indicators are used only for Passthrough-mode interception.
- A read-status interception indicator shall be asserted only when a read-status command is internally processed due to the status interception enable being set.
- A JEDEC interception indicator shall be asserted only when a Read JEDEC ID command is internally processed due to the JEDEC interception enable being set.
- An SFDP interception indicator shall be asserted only when a Read SFDP command is internally processed due to the SFDP interception enable being set.
- Once asserted, an interception indicator shall remain asserted until reset.

## 8. SPI IO Mode Output

The parser shall always report the SPI IO mode as single-lane IO. It shall not change the IO mode output.

## 9. Command Configuration Outputs

The command-configuration function is not active in this module.

- The command-configuration request output shall always be deasserted.
- The command-configuration index output shall reflect the five least-significant bits of the byte currently presented to the parser.

## 10. Reset and Idle Behavior

- On reset, the parser shall return to idle, select no datapath, clear the latched command information, and clear all interception indicators.
- In idle, the parser shall wait for a valid received byte before making any decision.
- After a byte has been classified, subsequent bytes in the same SPI transaction shall not change the selected datapath, the latched command information, or the interception indicators.
- The parser shall remain idle and non-active outside SPI Flash mode and SPI Passthrough mode.
